name: Mahalalel
overview: Mahalalel is a male figure in the genealogy recorded in Genesis, identified specifically as the son of Kenan. There is no tribal affiliation or additional notes provided about him beyond his lineage. His role is primarily genealogical, linking key ancestral lines in the early biblical narrative.
namesAndTitles: The name Mahalalel means 'praise of God [El],' reflecting a theocentric meaning that honors the divine. This proper name is recorded in Genesis 5:13 and is not indicated as given directly by God but carries a significant spiritual connotation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Mahalalel as the son of Kenan, as inferred from Genesis 5:13, and explicitly as the father of Jared in Genesis 5:15. These relationships place him within the early patriarchal lineage described in Genesis chapter 5.
scriptureSignificance: Mahalalel's significance lies in his position within the genealogical line tracing from Adam through successive generations. As the son of Kenan and father of Jared, he serves as a crucial link in the biblical ancestry that ultimately leads to later key figures. His inclusion in the genealogy emphasizes God's providential preservation of the line through which the Messiah would eventually come, highlighting God's faithfulness to His promises.
